content: Swedish American Hospital is a 357-bed, non-profit teaching hospital located in Rockford, Illinois. It is owned and operated by the Swedish American Health System. The hospital was founded in 1911 and officially opened its doors to patients in 1918 after a period of fundraising. In the mid-1990s, the hospital proposed a significant modernization and expansion of its campus. This proposal included a request to the city of Rockford to reroute Main Street, which ran through the middle of the hospital campus. The city agreed to this request on the condition that Swedish American would assist in revitalizing a nearby blighted neighborhood. The hospital acquired 31 properties in a six-block area south of its campus and committed $2 million to the project. By 2001, dilapidated structures in the area had been demolished, and the hospital, in collaboration with the city and Habitat for Humanity, began constructing new homes in the neighborhood. Concurrently, Swedish American Hospital initiated its own campus revitalization project, which included the opening of a $44 million, 94-bed heart hospital in June 2006. This facility enhanced the hospital's ability to treat cardiovascular diseases and gave the campus a modernized appearance. Between 2000 and 2006, the Swedish American Health System invested a total of $100 million in campus and neighborhood improvements. Swedish American Hospital serves the greater Rockford, Illinois region, which includes northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin. It is a teaching hospital affiliated with the University of Illinois College of Medicine. The hospital employs more than 350 physicians across 40 specialties and operates an outpatient surgery center that serves approximately 6,000 patients annually. Its emergency department is designated as a Level II Trauma Facility. Following the campus expansion, the hospital now consists of several interconnected structures. The main campus is bordered by East State Street (U.S. Route 20) to the north-northeast and East Charles Street to the south-southwest. The eastern boundary is marked by Ninth Street, while Williams Park lies to the west. Key buildings within the campus include the 94-bed heart hospital, a radiology and oncology center, Camelot Tower, the Renaissance Pavilion, two main wings, and additional peripheral buildings. The P. Johnson Building is located in the far northwest corner of the complex. The emergency room entrance is situated on the west side of the building and is accessible via a driveway that connects Charles Street to State Street. In terms of patient satisfaction, a 2005 survey revealed that 98% of Swedish American patients would recommend the hospital to their friends and family.
